Explain what a hash map is and why lookups are O(1).
response:
Ooo, hash map — favorite structure, honestly. 🌌

- Hash map = array + hash function. Key goes in, hash function turns it into a number, number = index in array. Value lives there.
- Lookup: compute hash, jump straight to that index. No scanning, no searching row by row. One jump, done. That jump is O(1).
- "Average" O(1), careful — good hash spreads keys evenly, few collisions. Bad hash, everyone piles into same bucket, becomes O(n) worst case.
